va_buttermilks_the.blurb: The Buttermilks is a cluster of boulders along a trail beside Riverside Drive on the south side of Richmond, inside James River Park. It is almost entirely bouldering, with a very large number of separate boulders each holding a handful of problems. The grades are friendly: plenty of easy and moderate problems from the lowest grades up through V5, then a thinner tail of harder lines reaching into the V8 range. Whale Boulder, Hidden Temple, Juicebox Boulder and the Biker Area hold the most problems. It is a city-edge spot, so it suits short sessions and visits spread across several different boulders.

ca_boulder_basin.blurb: Boulder Basin sits high in the San Jacinto Mountains, around 7,300 feet in San Bernardino National Forest, at the end of the Black Mountain road. It is a bouldering area, with a handful of roped trad lines on the side. Black Mountain's boulders are granite: grippy, sharp rock with thin edges, slopers and cracks. Problems run from easy slabs through steep, tall lines up to a hard top end, with a lot of moderates in the V0 to V3 range. Central Basin is the largest cluster, followed by South Basin, December Boulders and North Basin. Spring and fall are the favoured seasons on Black Mountain, while winter often brings snow.

ca_middle_earth_4.blurb: Middle Earth is the central valley of Fairview Mountain, a high-desert climbing area near Apple Valley at about 3,800 feet. It is overwhelmingly sport climbing, with a smaller amount of trad and a few top-ropes and boulders. Most routes fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with the largest group around 5.10 and a few lines up to 5.12. Fairview Mountain's rock is monzonite with a good patina, and this valley holds some of the longest climbs on the mountain. The main walls are Fairview Dome, Zena Rocks, Hercules' Foot and Presidents Crag. At Zena Rocks the cooler months from late fall to early spring suit the climbing best.

co_nine_mile_roped.blurb: Nine Mile Roped is the rope-climbing side of Nine Mile Hill in Unaweep Canyon, south of Grand Junction along CO 141. Sport routes lead, with a fair amount of trad and boulder problems mixed in. The roped grades run from about 5.7 to 5.11, clustering in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, and the boulder problems are mostly V1 to V4. The climbing on Nine Mile Hill is on the Burro formation, a sandstone that the canyon's boulders share. Four Blocks Crag is the biggest cluster by far, with Peter Wall, Grit Wall and Pet Wall making up much of the rest. The hill is better known for its huge field of boulders than for its roped walls.

_expect.name: Burr Pond State Park / Paugnut State Forest

ct_burr_pond_state_park_paugnut_state_fo.blurb: This is a bouldering area in Torrington, spread through the wooded hills of Burr Pond State Park and the neighbouring Paugnut State Forest, where hardwoods, white pine and hemlock grow among rocky ground. The boulders are pink granitic gneiss, solid and well featured, with fine to medium grain that gives good friction without being harsh on skin. Problems run from the very easy to V8, and the bulk sit between V0 and V4. The Pink Granite Maze, Motocross Valley Dark Tower, Walnut Mountain and Laurel Queen Boulder hold the most problems. Some steeper ground feels remote and trails can be faint or missing, so bring a map.
